verdict.rationale: Hightouch's core sync/reverse-ETL engine natively supports recurring, schedule-based (or trigger-based) jobs, and journeys/AI Decisioning agents include 'scheduling rules,' so recurring automation is a first-class capability. However, the AI-native (MCP) surface is documented to build audiences, manage syncs, and analyze performance in natural language, but no evidence explicitly shows the AI assistant setting or altering a sync's schedule/cron cadence via conversation. Missing for 10: explicit MCP/agent examples of creating or modifying a scheduled recurring job, and independent verification that AI-driven schedule changes work end-to-end.
